macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks mixed as technology shares weaken
items.summary: The S&P 500 slipped slightly in early Friday trading, while the Dow rose about 0.8% and the Nasdaq fell roughly 0.6% as chipmakers including Micron and Intel declined. The previous session ended with gains of 0.3% for the S&P 500, 1.1% for the Dow and 0.1% for the Nasdaq.[2]

items.title: Fed chair offers no guidance on October rate decision
items.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh declined to prejudge upcoming interest-rate decisions while emphasizing the goal of price stability. Markets interpreted his comments as reducing the likelihood of an October hike, with one market report putting the probability of a hold at 85%.[1][4]

items.title: U.S. wholesale inflation accelerates sharply
items.summary: The producer price index rose 6.3% year over year in September, up from 5.6% in August and marking its largest increase since December 2022. Higher inflation is increasing pressure on the Federal Reserve even as markets debate whether to hold rates this month.[1]

items.title: Import prices and industrial production strengthen
items.summary: U.S. import prices increased 1.1% in September, bringing the annual rise to 8.1%, while industrial production grew 2.2% year over year. The data point to persistent price pressure alongside firmer industrial activity.[4]

items.title: Asian markets recover after technology sell-off
items.summary: World shares were mostly higher after a technology-led decline in Asian stocks. Indonesia’s market plunged after MSCI warned it could downgrade the country from emerging-market status, raising concerns about capital outflows.[1]

items.title: Tesla rises after unveiling next-generation Roadster
items.summary: Tesla shares gained about 1.8% in early trading after the company unveiled a next-generation Roadster, although production is not expected until 2028.[4]

items.title: Travelers beats earnings and revenue expectations
items.summary: Travelers reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $9.18 per share, well above the $7.25 consensus estimate, while revenue reached $12.41 billion versus expectations of $11.31 billion. Despite the beat, the shares declined in early trading.[4]

items.title: European stocks advance on earnings and lower Fed-hike bets
items.summary: European equities rose as investors responded to positive corporate results and reduced expectations for an immediate Federal Reserve rate increase. Nordex shares jumped about 12% after the wind-turbine maker exceeded third-quarter expectations and raised its full-year margin target.[6]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $82,000 after sharp sell-off
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly fell below $80,000 after a hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation reading, then recovered above $82,000. Nearly $950 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated, while U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded more than $261 million in outflows.[2]

items.title: Celestia rallies as Eden AI-agent chain launches
items.summary: Celestia’s TIA token rose 57% over the week to approximately $0.75, its highest level since November 2025. The move followed the launch of Eden, an EVM-compatible chain designed for experimenting with AI agents.[1]

items.title: Injective gains on ETF and institutional-validator interest
items.summary: Injective rose about 25% over the week amid institutional attention, including 21Shares’ filing for an Injective ETF that would directly hold and stake INJ. Gulf Labs also joined the network as an institutional validator.[1]

items.title: NEAR falls sharply amid liquidations
items.summary: NEAR Protocol dropped 6.28% in four hours and was down 4.36% over 24 hours at approximately $4.94. Long liquidations totaled about $760,000 during the reported one-hour period.[6]

items.title: Australian crypto-platform capital rules remain under consultation
items.summary: Australia’s securities regulator is consulting on three capital models for crypto platforms. One proposed model would require platforms without qualifying outsourced custody to hold the greater of A$14 million or 10% of average revenue.[3]

items.title: NEAR Intents reports approximately $3.8 million security incident
items.summary: A vulnerability involving third-party contract interactions and a refund mechanism created roughly $3.8 million in false balances through 23 failed deposit transactions. The balances were later extracted through Omni’s cross-chain infrastructure.[4]

items.title: Bitcoin mining difficulty rises 5.92%
items.summary: Bitcoin’s mining difficulty increased 5.92% to 140.58 trillion at block height 971,712, according to mempool.space data cited in the report.[4]
